questions.statement: Read the text and identify its main idea: 'Volunteers planted forty trees along the river this spring. Local schools collected plastic and glass, and the river bank now looks completely different.'
questions.context: A reading comprehension exercise in a school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: A volunteer project changed the river bank
options.feedback: Both sentences describe the same project and the change it produced, which is the central idea.

options.text: Plastic and glass are dangerous for rivers
options.feedback: That is a general claim the text never makes; it only mentions the collection of waste.

options.text: Local schools dislike planting trees
options.feedback: The text shows the opposite: the schools took part in the planting effort.

options.text: Spring is the best season for planting
options.feedback: The season is mentioned once and is not the point the text develops.

questions.explanation: The whole text describes one project and its visible result, so the main idea is what the tree planting achieved along the river.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence best expresses the main idea of a text about a library that lends books and also runs reading clubs on Saturdays?
questions.context: A reading strategy lesson in a school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: Reading clubs are more useful than borrowing books
options.feedback: The text describes both without ranking them, so this adds a judgement it does not make.

options.text: The library lends books and organises reading clubs
options.feedback: This names both activities the text describes, which is what a main idea must do.

options.text: Saturdays are busy at the library
options.feedback: That is a single detail about one day rather than the idea the whole text supports.

options.text: Libraries should not lend books on Saturdays
options.feedback: The text gives no recommendation of that kind, so this contradicts the information.

questions.explanation: The main idea covers both functions described, so the best statement names the library and its two activities together.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read the passage and choose the main idea: 'Every morning before school, Ana walks her dog in the park. She has done this for three years and knows every regular there by name.'
questions.context: A reading comprehension task in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: The park is empty in the early morning
options.feedback: The text says she knows the regulars, which implies the opposite of an empty park.

options.text: Ana dislikes walking in the park
options.feedback: Knowing the regulars by name suggests she enjoys the routine, which is the opposite.

options.text: Ana keeps a daily morning routine with her dog
options.feedback: The habit of three years is the point of the passage, and both sentences support it.

options.text: Dogs should not be walked before school
options.feedback: The text makes no comment on whether the habit is appropriate.

questions.explanation: Both sentences describe Ana's long-standing morning routine with her dog and the familiarity it has brought.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the main idea of a text that explains how a school reduced its water use?
questions.context: A reading comprehension lesson in a school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: Water is a natural resource
options.feedback: That is a general fact stated anywhere, not the specific point the text develops.

options.text: Students should wash less often
options.feedback: No such recommendation appears; the text reports measures the school took itself.

options.text: Schools in the region use a lot of water
options.feedback: That would be a generalisation about many schools rather than this one's achievement.

options.text: The school managed to use less water
options.feedback: The purpose of such a text is to report a change achieved, which is the central idea.

questions.explanation: A text about reducing water use centres on the measures taken and the results they produced, so the main idea must include the change.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which detail is a main idea rather than a supporting detail?
questions.context: A lesson on main idea and detail in a school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: 'The panels were installed in April by a local company'
options.feedback: The date and the company support the main point but do not constitute it themselves.

options.text: 'The roof of the building was rebuilt'
options.feedback: This is a background fact about the building that does not express the point of the text.

options.text: 'The school has about six hundred students'
options.feedback: The number of students is context, not the central message about the panels.

options.text: 'Solar panels now supply the school's electricity'
options.feedback: This statement carries the purpose of the whole text and is not limited to one part of it.

questions.explanation: A main idea is the point the whole text serves, while a detail is one fact used to support it.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read and choose the main idea: 'The city closed several roads near the stadium so that thousands of fans could arrive safely on foot instead of driving.'
questions.context: A reading comprehension exercise in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: Thousands of fans came to the stadium that day
options.feedback: That is a fact mentioned in passing, not the point the sentence is serving.

options.text: Cars are dangerous in city centres
options.feedback: The text does not generalise about cars; it reports one specific measure on one occasion.

options.text: Roads were closed to keep fans safe on the way to the stadium
options.feedback: The action and its purpose are stated in one sentence, which makes it the central point.

options.text: The stadium should be moved out of the city
options.feedback: No such proposal appears anywhere in the text.

questions.explanation: The text gives a measure taken and the reason for it, so the main idea is about protecting fans around the stadium.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the difference between a main idea and a topic?
questions.context: A reading strategy explanation in an English class in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: They are two words for exactly the same thing.
options.feedback: The topic is narrower than the claim the text makes, so they are not identical.

options.text: The topic names the subject; the main idea states what is said about it
options.feedback: A topic is broad and a main idea is a complete claim about that subject.

options.text: The main idea is always the title of the text.
options.feedback: A title often hints at the topic, but the main idea is a statement, not a title.

options.text: A text has a main idea but never a topic.
options.feedback: Every text has a topic; the main idea is the extra step of stating a claim.

questions.explanation: The topic names the subject area of a text, while the main idea states what the text actually says about that subject.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read the text and choose the main idea: 'Many small farmers stopped using chemical fertilisers after learning that overuse had left the soil exhausted, and their harvests became cheaper and healthier.'
questions.context: A reading comprehension exercise in a school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: Small farmers changed their methods for better results
options.feedback: The cause and its two effects together form the central point of the passage.

options.text: Chemical fertilisers should be banned everywhere
options.feedback: The text reports a change of practice, not a general prohibition it advocates.

options.text: Farming is the most important activity in a country
options.feedback: That broad claim is not made anywhere in the passage.

options.text: Soil exhaustion is impossible to repair
options.feedback: The passage shows the opposite, since the harvests improved after the change.

questions.explanation: The text links a change in farming practice to two results, and that link is what the whole passage is about.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence states a main idea that covers the whole of a short text?
questions.context: A summarizing exercise in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: The roof of the theatre leaked for years
options.feedback: This covers only one part of the text and would leave the rest unexplained.

options.text: The text explains how the old theatre was restored
options.feedback: Every part of the text would contribute to that explanation, which is the test of a main idea.

options.text: The city restored several old buildings
options.feedback: This is broader than the text and would not identify what this particular text is about.

options.text: Restoration work can be very expensive
options.feedback: That is a general comment the text does not necessarily make at all.

questions.explanation: A good main idea must be true of the entire text, not only of the first or last sentence, and must state a complete claim.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read and choose the main idea: 'A small library that had only printed books began lending tablets as well, and soon elderly visitors who rarely read print were visiting every week.'
questions.context: A reading comprehension task in a school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: Printed books are no longer worth reading
options.feedback: The library kept its printed books, so the text does not argue for abandoning them.

options.text: Tablets are cheaper than printed books
options.feedback: No comparison of cost appears anywhere in the passage.

options.text: Elderly people cannot learn to use new technology
options.feedback: The text shows them using the tablets with ease, which contradicts the claim.

options.text: Adding tablets brought older readers to the library
options.feedback: The change and its effect on visitors form the connected central point.

questions.explanation: The passage reports a change and its effect on a specific group, and that is the claim the whole text supports.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read the text and choose its main idea: 'The council planted trees along the avenue, and during the following summer the temperature at midday was noticeably lower than before.'
questions.context: A reading skills lesson in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: Avenues are usually wider than side streets
options.feedback: The sentence compares widths, which the text never discusses.

options.text: Summer is hotter than every other season
options.feedback: The text mentions only one summer and makes no such comparison.

options.text: Planting trees lowered the temperature along the avenue
options.feedback: The action and its measured effect together form the central claim.

options.text: The council ignored the views of residents
options.feedback: Nothing in the passage suggests any disagreement with the public.

questions.explanation: The passage connects an action taken with a measured result, and that link is the point the whole text serves.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence would make the best topic sentence for a paragraph about the value of a school library?
questions.context: A reading skills lesson in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: A school library gives students access to resources they cannot easily find elsewhere.
options.feedback: It names the subject and opens a claim that several sentences can develop.

options.text: I went to the library on Tuesday afternoon at about four.
options.feedback: It reports one personal visit, which is too narrow to govern a paragraph.

options.text: The word library comes from the Latin word for books.
options.feedback: The etymology introduces a different subject from the paragraph's point.

options.text: Books are made of paper that comes from trees.
options.feedback: The sentence changes the subject to the raw material of books.

questions.explanation: A topic sentence must be general enough to be developed and must name the subject the paragraph will explain.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read and identify the main idea: 'Fewer students chose the optional computing course this year, and the teachers decided to review how it was advertised to beginners.'
questions.context: A reading skills lesson in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: Computing is not useful for most students
options.feedback: The text never evaluates the subject, only its uptake.

options.text: Teachers should stop offering optional courses
options.feedback: No such recommendation appears in the passage.

options.text: Advertising for courses is always ineffective
options.feedback: The text describes one case and draws no general conclusion.

options.text: Falling enrolment led to a review of how the course was advertised
options.feedback: The decline and the resulting decision form the connected central point.

questions.explanation: The text reports a decline and the response taken, and that combination is what the passage is about.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which detail is NOT part of the main idea of a text about a town that introduced a recycling scheme?
questions.context: A reading skills lesson in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: That most households now separate their waste
options.feedback: This shows how the scheme worked, which supports the main point.

options.text: The colour of the bins placed on the street
options.feedback: This is incidental information that the argument does not need.

options.text: That the amount collected each week has risen
options.feedback: The result confirms the scheme's success and belongs with the main idea.

options.text: That the council spent money on new vehicles
options.feedback: This explains how the scheme was carried out and supports the claim.

questions.explanation: A supporting detail explains or illustrates the main point, so it can be removed without destroying the central message.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: How would you summarise the main idea of a text that describes three different methods for reducing food waste?
questions.context: A reading skills lesson in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: It presents several practical ways of cutting food waste
options.feedback: The summary captures what all three methods have in common.

options.text: The first method involves storing bread in the freezer
options.feedback: That is one detail of one method, which a summary must generalise.

options.text: The third method was suggested by a shop nearby
options.feedback: The source of one suggestion is a detail, not the shared point.

options.text: Food waste has increased in the last ten years
options.feedback: That is a background claim the text does not necessarily make.

questions.explanation: A summary must cover the shared purpose of the methods described and leave out the detail of each individual one.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read and choose the main idea: 'Some students in the orchestra had never played an instrument, so the conductor ran two introductory sessions before the first rehearsal.'
questions.context: A reading skills lesson in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: The orchestra performed better than other orchestras
options.feedback: No comparison with other orchestras appears anywhere in the text.

options.text: Learning music is easier than learning a language
options.feedback: The text draws no comparison between music and language learning.

options.text: Introductory sessions were added to prepare new players
options.feedback: The problem and the measure taken together make the point of the passage.

options.text: The conductor did not enjoy working with beginners
options.feedback: Nothing in the passage expresses the conductor's feelings about beginners.

questions.explanation: The passage explains a difficulty and the practical step taken to overcome it, which is the central matter.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the best test of whether a sentence is the main idea of a text?
questions.context: A reading skills lesson in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: Whether it appears more than twice in the passage
options.feedback: Repetition of a word or phrase is not the test of a main idea.

options.text: Whether the rest of the text is needed to explain it
options.feedback: If the sentence needs all the others to make sense, it is the main idea.

options.text: Whether it is longer than the other sentences
options.feedback: Length has no bearing on whether a sentence states the central point.

options.text: Whether it contains the word used in the title
options.feedback: A text can name its topic in the title without repeating it word for word.

questions.explanation: A main idea must account for the whole text, and deleting the rest of the passage should leave the sense intact.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read and choose the main idea: 'The old cinema had been closed for years, and after a local group raised the money, its roof was repaired and it reopened with a small stage inside.'
questions.context: A reading skills lesson in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: A closed cinema was repaired and reopened by local effort
options.feedback: The transformation and the people behind it form the central narrative.

options.text: Small theatres are more popular than large ones
options.feedback: The passage draws no general conclusion about the size of venues.

options.text: Cinemas in the region have all closed
options.feedback: Only one building is discussed, so no regional claim is made.

options.text: Roof repairs are always expensive
options.feedback: The cost of repairs is not mentioned in the text at all.

questions.explanation: The passage traces a change in one building from closure to reopening, which is what the whole text is about.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is a supporting detail for a paragraph whose topic sentence is 'Public libraries give free access to knowledge'?
questions.context: A reading skills lesson in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: Knowledge is one of the most discussed ideas in education.
options.feedback: The general claim would sit better as a topic sentence than as support for one.

options.text: Libraries usually have more books than bookshops.
options.feedback: The comparison of stock levels does not illustrate free access to knowledge.

options.text: Members can borrow up to eight books at a time without paying anything.
options.feedback: The sentence shows how the free access described actually works in practice.

options.text: Some libraries close during the afternoon.
options.feedback: This describes opening hours and does not support the claim about free access.

questions.explanation: A supporting detail illustrates or proves the general claim made in the topic sentence.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read the paragraph and identify its main idea: 'The committee rejected the first design because the roof leaked. It approved the second design, which included new drainage and a steeper pitch, and construction began in March.'
questions.context: A reading skills lesson in a secondary school in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: Building committees should always meet in public
options.feedback: The text says nothing about how the committee conducts its meetings.

options.text: Steep roofs are more expensive to build
options.feedback: That detail about cost is never mentioned in the passage.

options.text: The first design was better than the second one
options.feedback: The text reports the opposite, since the second design was approved.

options.text: A second design was approved after fixing the leaking roof
options.feedback: The rejection, the change and the approval form the connected central point.

questions.explanation: The paragraph follows a design through rejection to approval, and the reason for the change is the point it develops.
questions.subject: ingles
